jurisdiction.venue: Full Federal Court of Australia, Melbourne

headline: Full Federal Court Refuses Appeal by Collapsed Derivatives Director Jailed Over A$681,497 Client-Fund Diversion
deck: Former Berndale Capital Securities director Stavro D’Amore must finish his 23-month prison term after failing to overturn his sentence for misusing company funds backed by retail deposits and falsifying overseas bank statements to Australia’s regulator.

live_updates.text: Full Federal Court refuses Stavro D’Amore’s application for leave to appeal his three-year, 10-month sentence (23 months to serve in prison).
A.S.I.C. Chair Sarah Court says the ruling confirms serious consequences for directors who abuse positions of trust and conceal misconduct.
Former retail clients of Berndale Capital Securities remain owed more than A$8.9 million nearly eight years after the O.T.C. derivatives broker collapsed.

financials.prison_display: 23 Mos Custody (3 Yrs 10 Mos Head Sentence)

score_provenance.rationale: Stavro D’Amore pleaded guilty and must serve 23 months of a 46-month prison sentence after losing his appeal, but faced A$0 in monetary fines on A$681,497 in diverted client-backed funds while former Berndale retail clients remain owed over A$8.9 million.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Full Federal Court refused former Berndale Capital Securities director Stavro D'Amore leave to appeal his 3-year-10-month sentence (23 months custody) after his guilty plea to diverting A$681,497 in client-backed company funds and submitting false overseas bank records to ASIC; clients are still owed A$8.9M.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Draining A$68,000 from a neighborhood credit union's customer deposit ledger and handing auditors forged foreign bank statements
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Multi-year custodial sentence with court-ordered restitution and asset confiscation
